title: OrbisTech POC scoping — open models & benchmarks
summary: Short scoping call to align on POC success criteria for OrbisTech's document understanding pipeline (financial reports + customer emails). Objective: pick an open-model shortlist, agree on benchmarks (latency / throughput / quality), size workload, and align a 4-week POC timeline. Key constraints: VPC/KMS, SOC2/compliance checks, multilingual support (EN/ES/PT), low hallucination requirements for extracted entities.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-20
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SA), Carlos (OrbisTech Head of ML), Priya (Platform), Liam (Product), Zara (Data Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Align on POC scope: benchmarks (latency/throughput/quality), shortlist open models, determine quantization/tradeoffs, multilingual requirements, 4-week timeline. Next: benchmark template + sample data.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, with Evan and Jordan from the solutions team. how's your morning Carlos?
[00:12] Carlos: hey, good, thanks. excited to dig in. quick ask up front — we need the POC to demonstrate both performance and extraction accuracy for financial docs, and we have to run inside our VPC with KMS keys.
[00:25] Evan: great, we can support VPC/private deployments. quick qualification — can you confirm expected throughput and latency targets, and languages?
[00:34] Carlos: target latency ideally p95 under 250ms for single-turn extraction, throughput around 50 requests per second during peak. languages: english, spanish, and portuguese for Brazil.
[00:45] Jordan: ok good, and are these synchronous API calls or batched jobs?
[00:49] Priya: mostly sync API from our microservices, but we might batch some backfill jobs. primary focus is sub-1s latency for user-facing flows.
[00:58] Maya: noted. success criteria — correct me if i'm wrong: 1) extraction accuracy above 92% F1 on your eval set; 2) p95 latency < 300ms (prefer <250ms); 3) cost estimate within your runway (we'll provide cost/per-token and per-request estimates); and 4) security/compliance checks complete. does that capture it?
[01:20] Liam: yes that's fair. also a small requirement — we need low hallucination on monetary values and legal clauses, can't have made up numbers.
[01:30] Carlos: exactly. in our last POC with another vendor there were hallucinated totals, that killed trust.
[01:36] Evan: understood. for hallucination mitigation we typically recommend 1) retrieval augmentation (RAG) for table/ledger lookups, 2) higher-quality models or fine-tuning on your domain prompts, and 3) constrained generation or structured outputs. we'll scope these in the POC.
[01:50] Zara: quick infra note — we require RBAC controls and audit logs for all inference calls and keys must be customer-managed in KMS.
[01:58] Jordan: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; we'll share the security doc.
[02:05] Maya: moving to models — Evan, could you run through the open-model shortlist and tradeoffs?
[02:10] Evan: yeah, so given your requirements — multilingual, finance domain, low hallucination — we suggest evaluating a small set of open models across quality/latency/cost: 1) Mistral-7B (smaller, fast, good L2 latency, can be quantized to int8/int4 but watch quality drop in int4), 2) Llama-2-13B-chat (strong general quality, decent multilingual, higher GPU memory), 3) Llama-2-70B-chat or similar big variants for top quality if you have Dedicated capacity, 4) Mistral-instruct or Mistral-large family (depending on availability), and 5) some community instruction-tuned models like OpenAssistant/oasst for larger context while keeping costs down.
[02:53] Carlos: curious — for Spanish/Portuguese, does Mistral handle those well or is Llama better?
[03:00] Evan: Mistral-7B is ok, but Llama-2-13B tends to have stronger multilingual ability in many benchmarks. For Portuguese, you might see Llama outperform smaller Mistral variants; that said, you can also fine-tune or use few-shot prompts to improve. We should run language-specific quality checks in the POC.
[03:18] Priya: and quantization — int8 vs int4 — what's the real-world impact?
[03:22] Evan: int8 usually gives a good tradeoff: ~30-40% memory reduction with minimal quality loss. int4 can double capacity but sometimes introduces hallucinations or numeric errors — not ideal for monetary fields unless we validate heavily. We recommend int8 for the initial POC and maybe evaluate int4 on non-critical paths.
[03:40] Liam: what about retrieval augmentation — do you plan to host embeddings locally?
[03:45] Jordan: yes we can index your sanitized docs into a vector DB in your VPC; Redwood supports connecting to customer-managed vector stores or we can host. For POC we'll likely run a small in-VPC index for low-latency retrieval.
[03:58] Carlos: great. benchmarking — what tests will you run?
[04:02] Evan: baseline plan: 1) latency: token-level and end-to-end p50/p95/p99; 2) throughput: sustained RPS with warm KV cache vs cold start; 3) quality: automated metric (F1 on extraction fields) + human spot checks; 4) hallucination tests: targeted prompts for monetary/legal fields; 5) memory/CPU/GPU util and cost-per-1M-tokens. we'll provide a spreadsheet template.
[04:29] Priya: please include cold-start measurements; our service scales up frequently.
[04:33] Evan: yes, we'll include cold vs warm cache results.
[04:36] Maya: timeline — typical Redwood POC is 4 weeks. here's our suggested cadence: week 0 (prep): data transfer, infra setup, security reviews; week 1: baseline runs on Mistral-7B & Llama-13B (int8) + ingestion; week 2: quality runs & multilingual checks, introduce retrieval; week 3: iterate on prompts/fine-tune small adapters if needed; week 4: final report + cost/production plan. does that work?
[05:05] Carlos: 4 weeks is fine. we have compliance windows that would like security review completed in week 0 — we'll prioritize.
[05:12] Zara: we can block time for security review next week, likely Tue/Thu.
[05:17] Maya: perfect. anything else on success metrics?
[05:20] Liam: one more — we need reproducible benchmark artifacts we can hand to platform team; raw logs, scripts, and the benchmark sheet.
[05:29] Evan: we'll share scripts and a reproducible harness, and we'll store logs in your S3 bucket in the VPC.
[05:35] Carlos: when you say 'reproducible', do you run the tests on Redwood Dedicated or hosted? we need to know parity with production.
[05:43] Jordan: for the POC we'll run on a private deployment (customer VPC) to reflect your network characteristics; if you want Dedicated we can mirror that as well. We'll note any differences in the report.
[05:53] Priya: ok good. are there model variants or fallbacks to discuss?
[05:57] Evan: yes typical pattern: primary model for quality (e.g., Llama-13B), fallback to smaller faster model (Mistral-7B) on high load, and a cached KV prefix layer for repeated queries. Redwood routing can do model fallback by policy.
[06:12] Carlos: what's the expected token cost differential between Llama-13B and Mistral-7B?
[06:15] Maya: rough ballpark — Mistral-7B can be 2-3x cheaper per-token execution costs, Llama-13B closer to 4-5x more expensive depending on instance type and quantization. we'll include a modeled cost sheet.
[06:30] Liam: any legal/procurement notes? we will need SOC2 attestation and data processing addendum before production.
[06:37] Maya: yes, we'll share SOC2 report and standard DPA; we'll also include details on key management and audit logs.
[06:44] Carlos: ok, what about timeline to spin up the VPC connectors? Priya?
[06:48] Priya: should be 3-5 business days if we get the network requirements. we'll try to have that ready by 2025-08-24.
[06:55] Maya: summary and next steps — we'll: send benchmark template and SOW; Evan will run baseline tests on Mistral-7B and Llama-2-13B in int8; Carlos to provide eval data; Priya to confirm VPC/KMS; schedule follow-up to align shortlist.
[07:12] Carlos: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:15] Maya: thanks — we'll follow up with links and the template.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors and speaker label inconsistencies; filler words preserved. Shared artifacts mentioned: benchmark template (https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/template), security packet (link to sent doc), SOW draft (link to be provided).
